explanation: The statement is about `ContinuousLinearMap.factorThru`, the library's own Douglas-factorization construction (defined in TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Gram/Factor.lean, line 106). Searching Mathlib for `factorThru`/`FactorThru` gives only unrelated category-theoretic notions (`Subobject.factorThru`, `Abelian.factorThruImage`, `Projective.factorThru`, `Limits.factorThruImage`, ...), and searching for `Douglas`, `PartialIsometry`, polar decomposition in Mathlib/Analysis turned up nothing about factoring bounded operators, so Mathlib contains no `factorThru` for continuous linear maps. I also examined Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Extend.lean (the `LinearMap.extendOfNorm`/`extendOfIsometry` API, including `extendOfIsometry_eq`, `extendOfIsometry_apply`, `norm_extendOfNorm_apply_le`) and Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace for dense-range isometry statements; none mentions `factorThru`, so none can state this result, and no single Mathlib declaration gives it by instantiation. The proof itself only applies the library's own `ContinuousLinearMap.norm_factorThru_apply` plus `DenseRange.closure_range`, so there is no Mathlib duplicate.
